results.title: [PDF] to addressing informality and promoting the transition to formality for ...
results.content: Formalization can be pursued through three complementary channels, which are the objectives of Recommendation No. 204: (i) facilitating the transition of workers and economic units from the informal to the formal economy, while ensuring respect for workers’ fundamental rights and ensuring opportunities for income security, livelihoods and entrepreneurship; (ii) promoting the creation, preservation and sustainability of enterprises and decent jobs in the formal economy and the coherence of macroeconomic, employment, social protection and other social policies; and (iii) preventing the informalization of jobs within the formal economy. For instance, in Iraq, following a diagnostic study, 180 the ILO has been providing a range of measures to support reducing informality and preventing informalization, including: (i) promoting the development of SMEs through streamlined business registration processes and an improved business environment; (ii) equipping workers with skills to access formal employment opportunities, such as vocational training programmes in green skills; (iii) engaging with different local actors to enhance infrastructure and create decent jobs in different sectors; and (iv) expanding social protection coverage.

results.title: How to support informal workers and economies in a just transition
results.content: While some cities are taking steps to include and recognise informal workers and economies in public service provision, informal sectors are often not considered in climate action or just transition plans. Here, we outline actions and considerations that can help cities to include informal workers in workforce planning and policy, improve working conditions and financial security for informal workers in the transition, and support the delivery of climate actions. **Collaborate with informal groups to build an evidence base on informal workers’ demographics, capacities and needs and to understand your city’s relationship with informal-sector actors.** Women, children, indigenous people, migrant populations and youth are often overrepresented in informal economies.7 Information about informal workers and their needs is key to their inclusion and to better-informed, supportive and protective policies. *City stories: Strengthening partnerships with informal workers to deliver a just transition* provides policy recommendations and case studies from Accra, Rio de Janeiro and Lagos for cities looking to strengthen and build partnership with their informal waste sector.
